Galahad. Sir Galahad stands as the purest and most virtuous knight of the Round Table, destined from birth to achieve what no other mortal could: the Holy Grail. As the son of Lancelot and Elaine, he represents redemption for his father's sin and the spiritual climax of Arthurian legend.

He was born of a magical deception orchestrated by enchantresses who desired Lancelot's strength to produce a perfect heir. The Siege Perilous, the seat at the Round Table reserved for the worthiest knight, was meant for him alone. Galahad undertook the Grail Quest, where his absolute purity allowed him to succeed where older, more worldly knights could not. He achieved the Holy Grail through virtue rather than strength or cleverness, transcending the martial tradition of Camelotry. He was said to be transported to Sarras, a mystical land, when he achieved the Grail, his mortal body transformed or taken to heaven.

Galahad represents the spiritual ideal toward which Arthurian chivalry aspired, even as the flawed reality of his father's affair undermined it. He was often depicted with a white surcoat and brilliant countenance, visibly marked as holy and set apart. He shares these bonds: Lancelot, his father, whose sin he redeems through perfect virtue. Percival, a fellow Grail seeker and a more flawed and human hero. The Round Table, the fellowship he served and elevated through his achievement. And the Holy Grail, the sacred relic only he was pure enough to attain.
